summary: Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter, and taught Sonam Kachru.

Godabarish Mishra (1886–1956) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. Educated at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta, he taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya (1913–1919), was headmaster at Chakradharpur High School (1919–1921), and directed at the University of Madras.

Gombojab Tsybikov (1873–1930) worked in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University (1895–1899), later serving as Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University (~1902–1917).
Gopal Lal Meena is an Indologist who taught Shagun Sinha. His career includes posts as Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Professor Emeritus at the University of Delhi (both attested 2026).

Gopinath Kaviraj (1887–1976) studied at Maharaja's College, Jaipur, and Allahabad University under Arthur Venis, Madhusudan Ojha, and Shashadhar Tarkachudamani. He served at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University as librarian (1914–1920), Principal (1923–1937), and Head of Yoga-Tantra (1964–1969).

Gordon D. Kaufman (1925–2011) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar educated at Bethel College, Northwestern, and Yale. He held posts at Pomona College, Vanderbilt University, and Harvard University (~1963–1995), serving as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity.

Gordon Hannington Luce (1889–1979) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at Dean Close School and Emmanuel College, Cambridge (~1908–1912), he served as a professor at the University of Rangoon from ~1912 to 1964.

Gordon Johnson (b. 1943) studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. In the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology, he served as President of Wolfson College, Cambridge (1993–2010), Cambridge's Deputy Vice-Chancellor (1974–2010), and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).

Gore Ouseley (1770–1844) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He served at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (~1810–1814) and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1823–1844).
Gottfried August Bürger (1747–1794) was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1768–1772) and later taught there (~1784–1794). He also taught August Wilhelm von Schlegel.

Gottfried Bernhardy (1800–1875) worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1818–1822), he held a post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from ~1829 to 1875.

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck (1762–1824) studied at Academic Gymnasium Danzig and the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1782–1786). A linguistics and history scholar, he held a post at Vilnius University from ~1804 to 1824.

Gottfried Hermann (1772–1848) was a linguistics scholar who studied at Leipzig and Jena. He founded the Griechische Gesellschaft (1799) and served at the University of Leipzig as Professor of Philosophy (1798) and Director of the Philological Seminar (1803–1848).

Gottfried Kinkel (1815–1882) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Bonn (~1831–1834). He held posts at the University of Bonn (~1837–1848) and ETH Zurich (~1866–1882).

Gotthilf Heinrich von Schubert (1780–1860) was a philosophy scholar. He studied at the universities of Leipzig (~1799–1801) and Jena (~1801–1803), and later held posts at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1819–1827) and the University of Munich (~1827–1853).

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner (1840–1899) studied at King's College London and Heidelberg. He taught at King's College, served as Principal of Government College Lahore (1864), founded the University of the Punjab, and later led the Oriental Institute, Woking (~1884–1899).
Gouriswar Bhattacharya (1924–2013) was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as a Lehrbeauftragter at the Free University of Berlin from approximately 1975 to 1995.

Govind Chandra Pande (1923–2011) studied under K. C. Chaṭṭopādhyāya. A scholar of history, Indology, and Buddhist studies, he served as Vice-Chancellor of Rajasthan and Allahabad universities, and chaired the Allahabad Museum and the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (1893–1983) studied at Elphinstone College and Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and A. C. Haddon. An Indologist, he headed the Department of Sociology at the University of Mumbai (1924–1959) and founded the Indian Sociological Society.

Govind Swamirao Gai (1917–1995) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India and the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), and as epigraphy consultant to the American Institute of Indian Studies.
